title: Unveiling the defects and charge-transfer engineering of a dual-site aliovalent-doped CuBi 2 O 4  semiconductor: an energy-efficient, visible-light-driven nanophotocatalyst
content: Herein, a dual-site aliovalent-doping strategy is developed by introducing Ba2+ at Bi3+ sites and Al3+ at Cu2+ sites in CuBi2O4, yielding CuBi2O4, Ba-CuBi2O4, and Al,Ba-CuBi2O4 through a hydrothermal route, which are characterized by XRD, Raman, FTIR, XPS, FESEM, UV-vis absorption, and EIS analyses. Ba2+ doping enhances defect engineering by increasing the Ovac/Olat ratio and creating defect states that trap electrons, thereby reducing electron–hole recombination, as evidenced by XPS and EIS. Ba incorporation also narrows the optical bandgap from 1.77 to 1.58 eV, expands the lattice parameters, increases crystallite size, reduces microstrain, and transforms the flower-like aggregates of pristine CuBi2O4 into elongated, rod-like bundles. Subsequent Al3+ incorporation provides a complementary structural correction to Ba2+ doping, further narrowing the bandgap to 1.46 eV while slightly reducing the Ovac/Olat ratio, but it remains higher than that of pristine CuBi2O4. Compared with Ba-CuBi2O4, Al and Ba co-doping increases microstrain and lattice distortion, transforming the elongated, rod-like bundles into compact microspherical assemblies of densely packed nanobars, resulting in the lowest interfacial charge-transfer resistance. Consequently, this sample achieves 98.25% methylene blue degradation under visible light after 90 min, with a first-order rate constant of 0.04381 min−1, approximately 2.12 times that of pristine CuBi2O4 (0.02062 min−1). Scavenger experiments reveal O2˙− and h+ as the dominant reactive species, with a secondary contribution from ˙OH, and after five cycles of reuse, Al,Ba-CuBi2O4 maintains 94.21% degradation efficiency. Thus, Ba and Al constitute a complementary dopant pair: Ba introduces beneficial defect-mediated functionality, while Al acts as a structural corrector, further optimizing the electronic and surface characteristics and enhancing photocatalytic degradation without substantially deviating from the parent lattice.
